content.text: The only MFN-style provision runs in our favour, so this rule is satisfied at the preferred position.

input.quote: 7.6 Vendor warrants that Fees charged to Customer will be no less favourable than fees offered to any similarly situated customer for comparable volumes and terms.
input.rationale: The only most-favoured-nation language in the Agreement is Clause 7.6, which runs in our favour: Vendor warrants that Fees charged to us will be no less favourable than those offered to similarly situated customers for comparable volumes and terms. Searches for "most favoured/favored", "no less favourable/favorable", "best pricing", "best terms" and "match" returned no other hits, and the candidate sections (§ 4 Order Forms, § 7 Fees, § 30 General) contain no obligation on Customer to extend best terms to Vendor or to match third-party offers. This meets the preferred position (no MFN obligation on Customer; a Vendor-granted MFN is welcome), so no redline is proposed. Separately noted for information only: Clause 7.7's late-payment liquidated damages is a burdensome payment term, but it is not an MFN issue and is addressed under the relevant payment/remedies rule.
